subject: Request: 5-year rate guardian sanction for ClearMed - exec signoff needed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 5-year rate guardian sanction for ClearMed - initial ask

Hi Naomi / Marissa —

Quick ask: ClearMed (healthtech payer) is asking for a five-year committed pricing schedule with a firm price floor and an uplift cap across the term. Key items: 
- Committed ARR: $4.2M over 5 years (annualized $840k).
- Requested: 25% off list Y1, then locked step increases capped at <=6% YoY uplift. They also want a renewal protection clause (first renewal cannot exceed Year5 net unit price + 6% uplift).
- They are sensitive to procurement timelines — procurement asked for an exec-signed pricing commitment to avoid re-tender.

Attachments: ClearMed_MA_v3_redlines.pdf (customer redlines), commit_schedule.xlsx (proposed phasing).

Why escalate: this is outside standard deal desk guardrails (multi-year fixed price + renewal guarantee). We need exec authorization for the economics and legal to accept the proposed renewal language.

Ask: Can we get conditional exec signoff (or an alternative set of guardrails) by EOD tomorrow so we can hit ClearMed's procurement deadline?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 5-year rate guardian sanction for ClearMed - initial ask

Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the numbers in commit_schedule.xlsx and the redlines. My read is: the commercial ask materially increases exposure if ClearMed under-utilizes their commit in later years. Two immediate mitigations we should require if execs are asked to bind: 

1) Minimum utilization tranche: 60% of committed tokens must be consumed in Year 1 or the uplift cap reverts to market rates (we can implement a true-up).
2) Annual cadence for quality & pricing review: lock economic uplift at <=6% YoY but include a bilateral termination window after Year 2 with a 90-day notice for material usage shortfalls.
3) Escrow for onboarding credits: hold 25% of year-1 discount in escrow to be released on attainment of usage milestones.

I recommend we escalate for an exec decision with those guardrails as required conditions. Please include legal's redline (Marissa) in the packet to send upward.

Ben — please confirm ClearMed will accept a usage milestone and escrow arrangement before I push this to Rishi + Marcus for signoff.

-naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Strategic Accounts (West)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: legal_redlines@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Oct 2025 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 5-year rate guardian sanction for ClearMed - legal summary attached

Naomi / Ben —

Legal reviewed the customer redlines (see attached PDF). Short summary of the problematic clauses: 
- Renewal protection as written would lock Redwood into below-market rates without a true-up mechanism — proposed change: limit renewal protection to a single renewal period and require usage-based true-up triggered if cumulative utilization <70% of committed volumes.
- Long-tail indemnities: push back on indefinite liability language; replace with Redwood standard 12-month cap and carve-outs.
- Early termination language: customer is asking for exit with 60 days' notice without financial penalties — we should require a pro-rated make-whole for the remaining committed term.

I've attached a redline that implements Naomi's suggested guardrails (min utilization tranche, escrow language, annual review, and make-whole). If the exec team wants to proceed we can bake these into the SOW and the commercial terms.

Attachments referenced: ClearMed_MA_v3_redlines.pdf (legal redline v1).

-M
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2025 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 5-year rate guardian sanction for ClearMed - request to Marcus for exec signoff

Looping Marcus for final signoff. My position: I support conditional approval provided we get the minimum utilization tranche and escrow mechanics, and that product/ops sign off on capacity planning (this account will be large on our shared GPU pools). If Marcus is fine with the escalation path and we document a hard true-up (and a single renewal protection window only), I'm comfortable routing to DocuSign.

Marcus — can you confirm you are comfortable with the proposed mitigation list below so we can finalize the commercial terms and present to ClearMed?

Proposed mitigation checklist: 
- 60% Year 1 minimum consumption requirement.
- Escrow: 25% of Y1 discount held for milestone release.
- True-up clause: if cumulative utilization <70% over the first 24 months, customer pays shortfall at market rate.
- Renewal protection: only covers first renewal; not a perpetual rate cap.

If yes, Marissa please prepare the final SOW + DocuSign packet.

-Rishi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2025 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 5-year rate guardian sanction for ClearMed - final signoff

I reviewed the mitigation checklist and the legal redline. I will approve the 5-year committed pricing package on the following binding conditions: 

1) The SOW must contain: minimum consumption (60% Y1), escrow mechanics (25% Y1 discount), a market-rate true-up if utilization <70% in first 24 months, and renewal protection limited to the first renewal only.
2) Product/ops must confirm capacity planning and provide written acknowledgment of the forecast impact within 48 hours of this email.
3) Deal desk may not accept further price erosion in subsequent negotiations without returning to me.

Upon receipt of a finalized SOW incorporating those items, you have my signature to proceed to DocuSign. Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
